takeaways: South Florida is about to set a construction-financing record: JPMorgan is leading a ~$1.3B package for Stern and Soffer's 800-unit Mercedes-Benz Places in Brickell, eclipsing Ross's $800M CityPlace deal — proof that money is available for the right sponsor and the right story.

Senior housing occupancy hit 89.9% in Q2, the 20th straight quarter of gains, with fewer than 16,000 units under construction nationwide. Demand keeps climbing while supply stays frozen — the strongest operating setup in a decade.
The Fed held at 3.50–3.75% on a 9-3 vote with three members pushing for a hike, killing the easy-money narrative. Underwrite for flat-to-higher financing costs, not for rate relief.

items.headline: JPMorgan Leads Record $1.3B Miami Construction Loan for Stern, Soffer
items.summary: JDS Development's Michael Stern and new equity partner Jeff Soffer of Fontainebleau Development are finalizing a roughly $1.3B financing package led by JPMorgan for the 800-unit Mercedes-Benz Places tower in Brickell, including a ~$250M C-PACE slug from Nuveen. It would be South Florida's largest-ever construction financing, topping Steve Ross's ~$800M CityPlace package. Walker & Dunlop's Aaron Appel and Jonathan Schwartz are running the process, with both sponsors co-guaranteeing and a close expected next month. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Senior Housing Occupancy Hits 89.9%, 20th Straight Quarter of Gains
items.summary: NIC MAP reports average occupancy across 31 primary markets reached 89.9% in Q2, up 40 basis points from Q1 and marking 20 consecutive quarters of growth. Fifteen of 31 markets are already at or above 90%, led by Boston (93.3%), San Francisco (92.7%) and Baltimore (91.8%). At the steady ~50 bps per quarter pace, industry-wide occupancy should clear 90% before year-end — a full recovery from the ~80% pandemic trough.

items.headline: Fed Holds at 3.50–3.75% on 9-3 Vote With Three Hawkish Dissents
items.summary: The FOMC kept rates unchanged at Chairman Kevin Warsh's second meeting, but the 9-3 split — with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all voting for a 25 bps increase — signals the next move may be up, not down. CRE borrowers counting on 2026 rate relief to refinance 2021-vintage debt should stress-test flat-to-higher scenarios instead.

items.headline: SEC Charges Tampa REIT in $150M Faith-Flavored CRE Fraud
items.summary: The SEC charged RAD Diversified REIT, run by Brandon "Dutch" Mendenhall and Amy Vaughn, with raising more than $150M from 5,500-plus investors under false pretenses while spending $5M+ on jewelry, jets and nightclubs. The firm touted 20% target returns and urged investors to tap IRAs, credit cards and home-equity loans, propping up sentiment with share valuations set by Mendenhall's brother. Over $50M allegedly moved to a private account; the REIT filed Chapter 11 in 2024. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Mamdani Rent Freeze Squeezes Bondholders on Teetering A&E CMBS Deal
items.summary: New York City's rent freeze is cutting into cash flow at A&E Real Estate's rent-stabilized portfolio, piling pressure on an already strained CMBS capital structure. A live reminder that regulatory risk can impair debt service faster than any operating miss — relevant to any operator underwriting rent growth in politically active markets. (via The Promote)

items.headline: LTC Properties Pushes 2026 Senior Housing Investments Toward $285M
items.summary: LTC Properties acquired a Wisconsin senior living community for $40M and forged a new operating relationship with Health Dimensions Group, bringing year-to-date SHOP investments to nearly $285M. REIT capital is clearly reopening to senior housing operating structures — a favorable backdrop for operators seeking recapitalization partners.

items.headline: Under 16,000 Senior Housing Units Under Construction Nationwide
items.summary: New senior housing construction remains near historic lows, with fewer than 16,000 total units under way as of Q2. With the 80+ population accelerating and no meaningful supply response, existing well-located communities hold pricing power that should persist for several years — the core thesis for stabilized acquisitions today.

items.headline: Blackstone, Brookfield Build Real Estate AI Tools In-House
items.summary: The largest owners are no longer waiting on proptech vendors — Blackstone and Brookfield are developing AI tools internally, from underwriting assistants to asset management copilots. For mid-sized owner-operators, the practical takeaway is that the competitive gap is now about proprietary data readiness, not software licenses.

items.headline: Stern, Soffer Clear G4 Note at Dolce & Gabbana Tower, Seek $650M
items.summary: The partners paid off the $46M acquisition loan on the Dolce & Gabbana-branded tower at 888 Brickell, squaring up with lender G4 Capital after the note had been shopped to debt investors including Beach Hill Capital. A term sheet is out for roughly $650M on the 250-unit project, even as JDS remains in litigation with Cottonwood Group over distressed Mercedes-Benz paper. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Avison Young Bank Accounts Frozen Over Tax Demand
items.summary: The brokerage had accounts frozen following a tax demand, per Bloomberg — another setback for a firm already mid-turnaround. Worth watching for anyone with active listings or valuation engagements at the firm, as service continuity risk is real. (via The Promote)

items.headline: National Healthcare Properties Closes $197M in Senior Living Buys
items.summary: NHP closed roughly $197M of acquisitions for its senior housing operating portfolio since late June, following a March RIDEA deal covering 13 assisted living properties across eight states with Discovery Senior Living as operating partner. RIDEA structures continue to be the preferred vehicle for REIT capital entering senior housing.

items.headline: Welltower Adds $98M of Chicago Senior Housing From Capitol Seniors
items.summary: Welltower bought Arbor Terrace Highland Park and Arbor Terrace Glenview for $58M and $40M respectively from D.C.-based developer Capitol Seniors Housing, continuing its Chicago repositioning. High-barrier suburban submarkets with limited new supply remain the clearest bid in the market.

items.headline: Discovery Retains 36 Communities as Ownership Changes Hands
items.summary: Discovery Senior Living acted as the "connective tissue" in HF Acquisitions Holding's purchase of 23 communities, retaining management on 20 it already ran and adding three new ones. Operator continuity is increasingly the deciding factor in transitions — a competitive advantage for platforms that can hold the census through a trade.

items.headline: Proptech VC Hits $16.7B as AI-Native Startups Take $4.5B Share
items.summary: Venture investment in proptech reached $16.7B in 2025, up 68% year over year, with AI-native companies capturing $4.5B — a 42% jump in share, roughly double the growth of traditional SaaS peers. Capital is concentrating in construction robotics, asset management and building-systems automation, the categories most likely to hit senior housing opex.

items.headline: AI Adoption in Property Management Jumps 20% to 58% in One Year
items.summary: Property management AI adoption nearly tripled from 20% in 2024 to 58% in 2025, but only 8% of companies have fully automated any single process. The gap between pilots and production is where the value sits — operators who finish one workflow end-to-end will outrun those running a dozen experiments.

items.headline: Big Tech Earnings Split Valuations as AI Debt Wave Nears Bond Market
items.summary: The latest round of Big Tech results pushed technology valuations in sharply divergent directions rather than lifting the group. WSJ's Telis Demos warns a tidal wave of AI-related debt is set to flood bond markets — a supply dynamic that could widen spreads across all corporate and CRE credit. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Snap Subleases 200K SF From Verizon at Vornado's Penn Plaza
items.summary: Snap is taking roughly 200,000 square feet of sublease space from Verizon at Vornado's Penn Plaza complex in Manhattan, adding another large tech tenant to the Penn District repositioning. Sublease absorption at this scale is one of the more encouraging office datapoints of the summer. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Struggling Colleges Raid Restricted Donor Funds to Pay Bills
items.summary: WSJ finds colleges in real financial trouble covering day-to-day operating expenses with endowment money donors had restricted for entirely different purposes, without their knowledge or consent. A cautionary tale in governance drift: when cash gets tight, controls erode quietly before they fail loudly. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Mastercard Names Ling Hai CFO in Leadership Reshuffle
items.summary: Effective August 3, Ling Hai — previously President of Asia Pacific, Europe, Middle East and Africa — became Mastercard's Chief Financial Officer as part of an alignment aimed at strengthening execution and deepening enterprise leadership experience. Elevating a regional operator into the CFO seat is a notable bet on commercial fluency over pure finance pedigree.

items.headline: 71% of Business Leaders Confident Despite Tougher Economy
items.summary: JPMorgan's 2026 Business Leaders Outlook finds 71% of leaders confident in their own company's performance, 73% expecting revenue growth and 64% expecting higher profits. New product and service launches lead growth strategies at 58% (up from 53%), with strategic partnerships rising from 43% to 49% — a build-and-partner posture rather than pure cost cutting.

items.headline: 89% of Workers Say Prioritizing Health Lifts Their Performance
items.summary: Wellhub's State of Work-Life Wellness 2026 finds 89% of workers perform better when they prioritize health, and companies embedding wellbeing into leadership and performance management report 20–25% higher productivity. With 90% of employees reporting burnout symptoms in the past year, this is an operational lever for high-turnover senior living frontline roles.

items.headline: Longevity Goes Mainstream as 2026's Defining Wellness Category
items.summary: Wellness forecasters point to longevity becoming a full lifestyle framework in 2026 — metabolic optimization, functional nutrition, strength training, restorative sleep and community connection — alongside a new emphasis on "emotional fitness." For senior living, this is the vocabulary prospective residents and their adult children are already using.

items.headline: Spider-Man Opens to $927M Globally, Second-Biggest Debut Ever
items.summary: Sony's "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" pulled an estimated $927M worldwide in its opening weekend, including a $355M domestic take — the largest of 2026 by a wide margin and the second-biggest global debut in history. A rare bright spot for a superhero genre that had been in a prolonged slump. (via WSJ 10-Point)
